correctness.rationale: All nonconstant tests are singleton leaf queries or suffix-of-spine-group queries. A shattered decision tree of depth d>=2 cannot use singleton leaf queries before the last level, forcing its first d−1 query levels to divide the groups into 2^(d−1) consecutive nonempty blocks each with at least two leaves. Conversely balanced suffix-threshold tests distinguish 2^floor(log2 K) qualifying blocks, followed by a final singleton leaf test in each block. Earliest-end exchange proves greedy K computation. Incomparability/ancestor containment precludes VC shattering of two vertices. Independent literal root-to-leaf-path version-space recursion checked all 255 positive ordered profiles of total leaves <=8 and the two order-sensitive eight-leaf witnesses.
